title: Introduction to Scientific Computing and Data Science
description: Introduction to computational methods and data science using Python. Numerical algorithms, optimization, Monte Carlo methods, data wrangling with pandas, exploratory data analysis, regression and classification. Emphasizes software engineering practices including object-oriented programming, modular design, version control, testing, and documentation.

title: Computational Methods for Scientists
description: Translating mathematical problem descriptions to computer programs. Introduction to Unix system.

title: Scientific Modeling and Machine Learning
description: Advanced computational methods and machine learning using Python, implemented from mathematical foundations. Monte Carlo methods, dynamical simulations, Bayesian inference, MCMC, Gaussian processes, neural networks with backpropagation. Students build research-grade implementations, transition to modern frameworks. Develops AI literacy and responsible use. Emphasizes professional software practices and performance optimization.

title: Introduction to Quantum Computing
description: Overview of quantum computing and quantum information. Quantum mechanics of spin systems and qubits; entanglement, superposition, and measurement. Basic quantum circuits and their applications and physical implementation. Quantum cryptography. History, potential applications, and near-future prospects.
notes: Not open to students with credit or concurrent enrollment in PHYS 581 or PHYS 681 or COMP 681.

title: Advanced Topics in Computational Science
description: Selected topics in computational science.

title: Seminar
description: An intensive study in advanced computational science.
notes: Topic to be announced in the Class Schedule.

title: Professional Development for Computational Scientists Seminar I
description: Lectures, discussion and activities to develop necessary skills to prepare for successful research-intensive careers in academia, industry, government, and other sectors.   This is a two semester course sequence.

title: Professional Development for Computational Scientists Seminar II
description: Lectures, discussion and activities to develop necessary skills to prepare for successful research-intensive careers in academia, industry, government, and other sectors.   This is a two semester course sequence.

title: Student Industry Immersion Seminar
description: Students and partners will interact and explore novel ideas, develop a dialogue that may seed new projects, pairings, sponsorships, or internships, and enable actionable opportunities by matching interested students with project concepts from CSRC partners.  Course is updated annually.

title: Scientific Computing
description: Parallel programming using message passing to include high performance computing and MPI language extensions.

title: Computational Database Fundamentals
description: Data-processing techniques, software, database design, implementation, and manipulation.

title: Applied Mathematics for Computational Scientists
description: Linear algebra, differential equations and stability theory, and analytical methods for partial differential equations within the context of computational science.

title: Seminar: Problems in Computational Science
description: Applications of computational science in solving problems using a variety of methods. Problems selected from biology, chemistry, physics, and other fields.

title: Problem Solving Techniques
description: Data abstraction and problem solving skills.

title: Quantum Computing
description: Overview of quantum computing and quantum information. Quantum mechanics of spin systems and qubits; entanglement, superposition, and measurement. Basic and intermediate quantum circuits and their applications and physical implementation. Quantum cryptography. Simulation of quantum circuits. History, potential applications, and near-future prospects.
notes: Requires use of Python programming. Not open to students with credit or concurrent enrollment in COMP 581 or PHYS 581 or PHYS 681.

title: Selected Topics in Computational Science
description: Intensive study in specific areas of computational science.
notes: See Class Schedule for specific content. Credit for 596 and 696 applicable to a master’s degree with approval of the graduate adviser.

title: Research
description: Research in computational science.

title: Special Study
description: Individual study.

title: Thesis or Project
description: Preparation of a project or thesis for the master’s degree.

title: Thesis or Project Extension
description: Registration required in any semester or term following assignment of RP in Course 799A in which the student expects to use the facilities and resources of the university; also student must be registered in the course when the completed thesis or project is granted final approval.

title: Comprehensive Examination Extension
description: Registration required of students whose only requirement is completion of the comprehensive examination for the master’s degree. Registration in 799C limited to two semesters.

title: Seminar
description: Topics in different areas of computational science.

title: Colloquium in Computational Science
description: Discussions on advances in computational science research. Course to be taken every semester.

title: Supervised Research, Qualifying Examination, and Dissertation Proposal
description: Research and preparation for qualifying examination.

title: Practicum
description: Independent investigation in general area of field of dissertation. Conducted in industry or national laboratory under faculty supervision.

title: Doctoral Research
description: Independent investigation in general field of dissertation.

title: Doctoral Special Study
description: Individual study leading to study and research required for doctoral dissertation.

title: Doctoral Dissertation
description: Preparation of the dissertation for the doctoral degree. Enrollment is required during the term in which the student plans to graduate.
